title: Survey nonresponse can make income look higher and poverty look lower even when year-to-year direction is mostly preserved
source_unit: U.S. Census Bureau CPS ASEC administrative-record nonresponse-bias evaluation

observations.period: CPS ASEC survey years 2017-2026; 2026 evaluation published September 15, 2026

denominator.unit: CPS ASEC survey and linked occupied-address comparison frame; percentage and percentage-point measures are source-defined

weighted_response_rate_2026.unit: percent weighted CPS ASEC response rate in 2026

survey_only_income_upward_bias_since_202.unit: difference between survey-only and nonresponse-adjusted income estimates across the distribution

median_income_bias_2026.unit: percent by which survey-only median income exceeded the alternative nonresponse-adjusted estimate

poverty_rate_difference_2026.unit: percentage points by which the survey-only poverty rate was lower than the alternative-weight estimate

directional_trend_bias.value: year-to-year income and poverty changes were generally not significantly biased except for the 2019-2020 comparison

observations.method: Census linked CPS ASEC responses to IRS earnings and income records, SSA Numident, the 2010 Census, and American Community Survey information; it compared standard survey-only estimates with alternative nonresponse-adjusted weights.
observations.uncertainty: Linked administrative data can only correct differences observed in the linked fields. Census describes the alternative weights as a benchmark for evaluating bias, not definitive truth; the 2026 adjustment uses 2024 records because 2025 administrative records were unavailable.
observations.subgroup: CPS ASEC respondents and nonrespondents compared through occupied-address and linked administrative records; the source reports distribution-wide and all-family estimates rather than a complete causal subgroup account.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower response rates do not automatically create bias if respondents and nonrespondents are similar. The stable post-2020 bias means many year-to-year directions remain usable even though levels are shifted; adjusted estimates may also retain unmeasured bias.

related_sources.claim: CPS ASEC technical documentation supplies the survey design and weighting context for the nonresponse evaluation.

boundary: This record establishes a measurement and nonresponse-bias boundary for national CPS ASEC income and poverty estimates. It does not identify each nonrespondent's experience, establish the true population values, or invalidate every year-to-year trend.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Census Research Matters page retrieved and URL hash recorded; linked microdata and alternative weights are not retained
